series.title: Before the Gods: The Beginning of Everything

episodes.title: Before the Beginning: The Great Void Called Ginnungagap
episodes.covers: The primordial gap between the realms of ice and fire, and the strange conditions from which the world emerges.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

script.title: Before the Beginning: Ginnungagap
script.description: Before the gods, before the earth, there was a yawning gap between a world of ice and a world of fire. The Norse story of how everything began, as a disguised king heard it in a hall of shields.

episodes.title: Ymir: The Giant Whose Body Became the World
episodes.covers: The first primordial giant, his origins, and the extraordinary birth of the earliest beings.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Audhumla: The Cosmic Cow Who Revealed the First God
episodes.covers: The mysterious cow whose milk nourishes Ymir and whose licking of the ice reveals Buri.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Odin and His Brothers: The Murder That Created the World
episodes.covers: Odin, Vili, and Ve defeat Ymir and transform his body into the landscape of the cosmos.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: How the Gods Created the First Humans
episodes.covers: Ask and Embla, the creation of humanity, and the gifts that make human life possible.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Yggdrasil: The World Tree That Holds the Cosmos Together
episodes.covers: The great ash tree, its roots and wells, and the beings that live around or threaten it.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Nine Realms: A Journey Through the Norse Universe
episodes.covers: Asgard, Midgard, Jotunheim, and the other realms, with a note that the surviving sources do not provide one perfectly consistent map.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Norns: The Three Beings Who Shape Destiny
episodes.covers: Urd, Verdandi, and Skuld, their association with fate, and the relationship between destiny and the gods.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The First War: The Aesir and Vanir Clash
episodes.covers: The conflict between the two divine groups, its mysterious causes, and the settlement that follows.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Golden Age of the Gods: Why Peace Could Not Last
episodes.covers: The early prosperity of the gods, the arrival of new threats, and the first signs of the disasters to come.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

series.title: The Rise of the Gods and the Defences of Asgard

episodes.title: Asgard: The Fortress of the Gods
episodes.covers: The home of the Aesir, their halls, their councils, and the meaning of divine power.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Valhalla: Odin's Hall of the Slain
episodes.covers: The warriors chosen by the Valkyries, their life in Odin's hall, and their preparation for the final battle.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Builder of Asgard's Wall: The Deal That Nearly Cost the Gods Everything
episodes.covers: The mysterious builder, the impossible deadline, the horse Svadilfari, and Loki's intervention.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Birth of Sleipnir: How Loki Became the Mother of an Eight-Legged Horse
episodes.covers: Loki's transformation, the birth of Sleipnir, and the horse that becomes Odin's extraordinary mount.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Mead of Poetry: How Odin Stole the Gift of Inspiration
episodes.covers: Kvasir's death, the creation of the magical mead, and Odin's dangerous quest to acquire it.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Idunn and the Golden Apples That Kept the Gods Young
episodes.covers: Idunn's apples, the gods' dependence on her, and the crisis caused by her abduction.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Theft of Thor's Hammer: How the Gods Nearly Lost Their Greatest Weapon
episodes.covers: The giant Thrym steals Mjölnir and demands Freyja as his bride, forcing Thor into a humiliating disguise.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Wedding of Thor: The Battle Hidden Beneath a Bridal Veil
episodes.covers: Thor poses as Freyja, retrieves his hammer, and turns the wedding feast into a battle.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Master Smiths: The Treasures Forged for the Gods
episodes.covers: The dwarven craftsmen and the creation of Mjölnir, Draupnir, Gungnir, and other legendary treasures.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Walls of Asgard: Why the Gods Could Never Feel Completely Safe
episodes.covers: Revisit the gods' defences, their enemies, and the growing awareness that their security is temporary.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Odin: The Allfather Who Sacrificed Everything for Wisdom
episodes.covers: Odin's pursuit of knowledge, his missing eye, his ravens, and his willingness to pay terrible prices for understanding.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor: The Thunder God Who Protected Humanity
episodes.covers: Thor's strength, Mjölnir, his role as a defender against giants, and his surprisingly comic adventures.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Freyja: The Goddess of Love, Magic, and War
episodes.covers: Freyja's associations with desire, seiðr magic, gold, and the warriors she receives after battle.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Freyr: The God Who Traded His Sword for Love
episodes.covers: Freyr's connection with fertility and prosperity, his love for Gerðr, and the consequences of surrendering his weapon.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Tyr: The God Who Sacrificed His Hand
episodes.covers: Tyr's connection with courage and law, and the deception required to bind Fenrir.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Heimdall: The Watchman Who Never Sleeps
episodes.covers: Heimdall's extraordinary senses, his role guarding the Bifrost, and his part in Ragnarök.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Frigg: The Queen Who Knew More Than She Could Reveal
episodes.covers: Frigg's position among the gods, her knowledge of fate, and her desperate efforts to protect Baldr.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Baldr: The Beloved God Whose Death Began the End
episodes.covers: Baldr's dreams, the efforts to protect him, Loki's plot, and the tragedy that shakes the divine world.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Hel: The Ruler of the Realm of the Dead
episodes.covers: Hel's origins, her domain, and the distinction between her realm and the warriors' destinations associated with Odin and Freyja.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Bragi, Idunn, and the Gods Who Guard Memory and Youth
episodes.covers: Poetry, storytelling, renewal, and the place of lesser-known deities in the divine community.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

series.title: Loki: The Trickster Who Helped Destroy the Gods

episodes.title: Who Is Loki? The God Who Never Belonged Anywhere
episodes.covers: Loki's giant ancestry, his relationship with Odin and the Aesir, and his shifting role as helper and adversary.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Loki and the Golden Hair: The Mischief That Created the Gods' Greatest Treasures
episodes.covers: Loki cuts Sif's hair and must arrange for the dwarves to create replacements and other magical treasures.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Loki's Strange Children: Fenrir, Jörmungandr, and Hel
episodes.covers: The prophecies surrounding Loki's offspring and the gods' attempts to control their dangerous futures.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Binding of Fenrir: Why Tyr Lost His Hand
episodes.covers: The growing wolf, the gods' fear, the magical chain Gleipnir, and Tyr's sacrifice.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Jörmungandr: The Serpent That Circled the World
episodes.covers: The World Serpent's growth, its place in the ocean, and its destined confrontation with Thor.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Loki and the Death of Baldr
episodes.covers: The mistletoe, Hodr, the fatal trick, and the moment Loki's relationship with the gods becomes irreparably damaged.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Loki's Punishment: Bound Beneath the Poisonous Serpent
episodes.covers: The gods' revenge, Loki's bonds, Sigyn's loyalty, and the mythological explanation associated with earthquakes.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Loki at Ragnarök: The Trickster's Final Betrayal
episodes.covers: Loki's release, his return against the gods, and his final confrontation with Heimdall.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

series.title: Giants, Monsters, Dwarves, and Magical Beings

episodes.title: The Jötnar: Were the Giants Really the Gods' Enemies?
episodes.covers: The giant families, their relationships with the gods, and why giants can be enemies, ancestors, lovers, or sources of wisdom.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Dwarves: The Master Craftsmen Beneath the Earth
episodes.covers: Dwarven craftsmanship, magical objects, and their role in shaping the fortunes of gods and heroes.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Valkyries: Odin's Choosers of the Slain
episodes.covers: The supernatural women who select fallen warriors and carry them to their destinations.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Einherjar: The Warriors Preparing for the End of the World
episodes.covers: The chosen dead in Valhalla, their daily battles and feasts, and their role in Odin's preparations.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Draugr: The Restless Dead of Norse Legend
episodes.covers: Undead guardians of graves and treasure, the threats they pose, and their place in later saga literature.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Níðhöggr: The Dragon Gnawing at the Roots of the World
episodes.covers: The creature beneath Yggdrasil, its associations with destruction, and the imagery of cosmic decay.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Eagle, the Squirrel, and the Stag: The Strange Life of Yggdrasil
episodes.covers: Ratatoskr, the eagle, Níðhöggr, and the creatures that inhabit or trouble the world tree.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Huldra, Land Spirits, and Hidden Folk
episodes.covers: Later Scandinavian folklore about supernatural beings, with clear distinctions between folklore and the older Eddic myths.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Magical Objects of Norse Mythology
episodes.covers: Mjölnir, Gungnir, Draupnir, Skíðblaðnir, and other objects whose powers change the course of stories.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Monsters of Ragnarök: Who Will Destroy the Gods?
episodes.covers: Fenrir, Jörmungandr, the fire giant Surtr, and the forces that converge at the end of the world.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor's Journey to Útgarða-Loki: The Challenges No One Could Win
episodes.covers: Thor, Loki, and their companions arrive at a giant's stronghold and discover that their contests are built on illusions.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor Tries to Lift a Cat: The Secret Behind an Impossible Challenge
episodes.covers: Thor's humiliating contest with a cat that is actually connected to the Midgard Serpent.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor and the Old Woman Who Defeated Him
episodes.covers: Thor wrestles Elli, old age personified, and discovers the limits of even divine strength.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor's Fishing Trip: The Day He Nearly Caught the World Serpent
episodes.covers: Thor and the giant Hymir go fishing, and Thor hooks Jörmungandr in one of the most dramatic encounters in Norse mythology.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor and the Giant Hrungnir: The Duel That Shook the Heavens
episodes.covers: The challenge posed by Hrungnir, the duel, and the strange weaponry involved in Thor's victory.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor and Geirröd: The Journey into a Giant's Trap
episodes.covers: Loki's involvement, the perilous journey, and the objects that help Thor survive Geirröd's attempts to kill him.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor's Journey to the Land of the Giants
episodes.covers: A connected exploration of Thor's journeys into Jötunheim and the recurring struggle between strength and cunning.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Giant Who Challenged the Gods to a Contest
episodes.covers: Revisit the themes of trickery, illusion, and how giants expose the limitations of the gods.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor, Loki, and the Price of Their Adventures
episodes.covers: How the gods' victories often come through bargains, disguises, and unexpected consequences.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor's Final Battle: The Serpent That Will Kill the Thunder God
episodes.covers: The prophecy of Thor and Jörmungandr's final encounter, leading directly into Ragnarök.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

series.title: The Legendary Heroes: Dragons, Cursed Gold, and Broken Oaths

episodes.title: The Völsungs: The Family Marked by Destiny
episodes.covers: The ancestry of the Völsung family, the sword Gram, and the heroic legacy inherited by Sigurd.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: Sigmund and the Sword in the Tree
episodes.covers: The mysterious sword embedded in a tree, the challenge to claim it, and the beginning of the family's tragedies.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: Sigurd the Dragon-Slayer: The Quest for Fafnir's Gold
episodes.covers: Sigurd's training, his encounter with the dragon Fafnir, and the acquisition of the cursed treasure.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: The Dragon's Blood: The Secret That Gave Sigurd Wisdom
episodes.covers: Sigurd's encounter with the dragon's blood, the birds' warnings, and the knowledge that changes his fate.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: Brynhild: The Valkyrie Who Fell into an Endless Tragedy
episodes.covers: Brynhild's origins, her punishment, and her relationship with Sigurd in the surviving traditions.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: The Broken Promise: How Sigurd Lost Brynhild
episodes.covers: Deception, magic, marriage agreements, and the chain of events that turns love into betrayal.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: Gudrun: The Woman Caught Between Love and Revenge
episodes.covers: Gudrun's marriage to Sigurd, the murder that transforms her life, and her response to devastating loss.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: The Murder of Sigurd: Why the Greatest Hero Had to Die
episodes.covers: The conspiracy against Sigurd, the conflicting motives of those closest to him, and the collapse of the Völsung household.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: The Cursed Gold of Andvari: Wealth That Brings Only Destruction
episodes.covers: Andvari's treasure, the ring Andvaranaut, and the curse that follows the gold through generations.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: Atli and the Niflungs: The Feast That Became a Massacre
episodes.covers: Gudrun's later marriage, the invitation that conceals a trap, and the destruction of the Niflung warriors.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: Gudrun's Final Revenge
episodes.covers: Gudrun's response to Atli's crimes and the extreme revenge that concludes this part of the heroic cycle.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

episodes.title: The Völsung Saga: Why No One Could Escape the Curse
episodes.covers: Connect the major events, family betrayals, and fatal choices that define the Völsung legend.
episodes.source: The Saga of the Volsungs (William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson translation, 1888) and the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda (Bellows, 1923)

series.title: Ragnarök: The Twilight of the Gods

episodes.title: Ragnarök: The Prophecy That Haunted the Gods
episodes.covers: The meaning of the gods' fate, the warnings in Völuspá, and why the end cannot simply be prevented.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Fimbulwinter: The Three Winters Before the End
episodes.covers: The terrible winters, social collapse, and the signs that the world's final crisis has begun.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Breaking of Bonds: Fenrir and Loki Are Released
episodes.covers: The release of imprisoned forces, the collapse of restraints, and the gathering of the gods' enemies.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: The Ship of the Dead: Naglfar Sets Sail
episodes.covers: The ship associated with the final conflict, the forces assembling against the gods, and the approach of the last battle.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Heimdall Sounds the Gjallarhorn
episodes.covers: The signal that summons the gods, the awakening of the final battle, and the collapse of the boundary between worlds.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Odin vs Fenrir: The Death of the Allfather
episodes.covers: Odin confronts the monstrous wolf and falls in the battle foretold for him.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Thor vs Jörmungandr: The Last Battle of Thunder and Serpent
episodes.covers: Thor kills the World Serpent but succumbs to its venom after taking his final steps.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Loki vs Heimdall: The Final Duel
episodes.covers: The ancient antagonists face one another in the destruction of the divine order.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: Surtr's Fire: The Burning of the World
episodes.covers: The fire giant's role, the destruction of the old world, and the collapse of the familiar cosmos.
episodes.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923) and Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda (Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur translation, 1916)

episodes.title: After Ragnarök: The World That Rises Again
